text: Israel complained all the way from Egypt to Sinai, and not one of them died. Every complaint was met with fresh supply.
explanation:
At the Red Sea they grumbled, "Did you bring us out here to die?" God parted the sea. At bitter Marah they complained, and God showed Moses a tree that made the waters sweet. They murmured about food, and God rained down manna. They quarrelled over water, and God brought it out of a rock. Not a single person died, because God was dealing with them on the basis of His covenant with Abraham: grace.

Then at Sinai, before the Ten Commandments were even spoken, they declared, "All that the Lord has spoken we will do." From then on, the same sin of murmuring brought death. Nothing changed in their behaviour. What changed was the covenant they'd put themselves under.

text: "Sin is not imputed when there is no law." The law brought the knowledge of sin, and with that consciousness came death.
explanation:
Paul makes a striking point: sin was in the world long before Moses, "but sin is not imputed when there is no law." In those generations people lived for hundreds of years, even with sin around them, because there was no law to make them conscious of it. "By the law is the knowledge of sin."

The tree in Eden was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, a picture of the law: knowing what's right, and finding you can't do it. "The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law." That's why sin has no dominion over those who are "not under law but under grace." God wants you living by the tree of life, which is Christ.

text: Cleansed worshippers "would have had no more consciousness of sins." Under the law there was "a reminder of sins every year."
explanation:
If the old sacrifices had really worked, "the worshippers, once purified, would have had no more consciousness of sins. But in those sacrifices there is a reminder of sins every year." The word for reminder is the same Greek word Jesus used at the Last Supper: "Do this in remembrance of Me."

Many think the church needs more sin-consciousness, and more sermons exposing sin. But that's the old covenant's annual reminder. The new covenant has a new remembrance: not your sins, but Him, your righteousness, holiness and life. You've been cleansed once and for all. Be conscious of Jesus.

text: The red heifer's ashes were for anyone who touched death. You can touch death without knowing it. Wash in the Word.
explanation:
Outside the five offerings of Leviticus, the book of Numbers adds one more: a red heifer burned to ashes, mixed with running water, cedar wood and hyssop. It wasn't for sin; it was for those defiled by touching a dead body. Placed in Israel's wilderness journey, it pictures Christ's finished work applied to us day by day as we walk through this world.

Once, in a bookstore, Joseph Prince leafed through a bestselling self-help book full of New Age ideas. Walking away, a severe headache came on. The Lord told him, "You touched death." The remedy wasn't a new sacrifice, but washing his mind with the water of the Word. Be careful what you take in, and keep washing.

text: In a yoke, the young ox learns from the older one: rest when He rests, drink when He drinks.
explanation:
"Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy and My burden is light." Farmers yoked a young ox to an experienced one. If the young one pulled against the older, it only hurt its own neck. It learned by keeping in step.

When the Lord says rest, rest, even if you're forced to stay home. When He prompts you to open His Word, do it then, not after the show; you may find the moment has passed. Flow with Him. His yoke is easy.

text: While Abraham climbed one side of Moriah, the ram was climbing the other. "The Lord will see to it."
explanation:
Abraham and Isaac climbed Mount Moriah not knowing how God would provide. But the ram caught in the thicket didn't just appear out of nowhere. It was making its way up the other side of the mountain the whole time. Abraham named the place Jehovah Jireh: literally, "the Lord will see." When someone says, "I'll see to it," they mean they'll provide.

God foresees your need long before you feel it. If hard times are coming in your job or finances, He has already provided. The supply is on its way up the other side of your mountain.

text: "Hearken, hearken." Listen with your outward ears and your inward ears, and expect to be made whole.
explanation:
"If you diligently obey the voice of the Lord… all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you." In Hebrew, "diligently obey" is the word hearken said twice. Hear with your ears, and hear with your heart. Turn off distractions, tell others it can wait, and give your full attention.

Don't wait until the end of a sermon to receive. God has chosen preaching to save, sozo, which also means to heal and make whole. "Receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls," your mind and emotions. As you hear His Word, expect anxieties to lift and your body to be made well.
